title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Morgan Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This document consolidates Redwood's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expense processing, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended for managers, people-ops, security, finance, and all employees who execute or rely on these processes.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all Redwood employees, contractors, and temporary workers across hosted, dedicated and private deployment teams. Exclusions or customer-specific deviations must be recorded and approved by the relevant owner team and security.

Owners and point-of-contact
--------------------------
- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.com
- Security (access & data oversight): security@redwood.com
- Finance (procurement, expenses): finance@redwood.com
- Legal (vendor contracts): legal@redwood.com

1) Access & permissions
-----------------------
Goal: Ensure least-privilege access, auditable approvals, and timely deprovisioning.

Principles:
- Role-based access where possible; account-level exceptions must be justified and time-limited.
- Access is approved by the requester's manager and a technical owner.
- All privileged access actions are logged and reviewed quarterly.

Process (request -> approval -> provisioning):
1. Submit request via Access Request form in the internal portal (link: /access-requests). Include business justification, required duration, and required access scope.
2. Manager approves the business justification.
3. Technical owner (system/service owner) approves scope and potential risks.
4. IAM team implements access and records ticket.
5. Request auto-escales to security review if elevated privileges or external network access requested.

Deprovisioning:
- Offboarding checklist triggers immediate disable of cloud/SSO access on termination or role change.
- Contractors: access expiration set at onboarding and automatically revoked.

SLOs and thresholds:
- Standard access requests: provision within 2 business days.
- Emergency access (time-limited elevated): approval within 4 hours. All emergency access must have retrospective review.

Auditing & Reviews:
- Quarterly access reviews led by Security; managers must attest to each active entitlement.
- Quarterly privileged user review with remediation tracking.

2) Change management
--------------------
Goal: Minimize risk from infrastructure, configuration, and production code changes while enabling fast delivery.

Scope: infra changes, runtime configuration, deployment rollouts, schema migrations, and major product releases. Routine code pushes that follow CI/CD standards are tracked but follow a lightweight flow.

Change types and approval matrix:
- Standard (low-risk): config toggles within documented ranges — owner approval.
- Normal (medium-risk): infra changes, non-breaking schema changes — manager + change board review.
- Emergency (high-risk): production outage fixes — on-call + incident commander approval, retro postmortem required.

Process:
1. Create a Change Request in the change-management system (PRD/Confluence template + ticket link). Include rollout plan, rollback plan, blast radius, verification steps, and owners.
2. Risk classification and assignment to CAB (Change Advisory Board) for Normal changes. Standard changes use fast-track.
3. Schedule change windows; notify stakeholders at least 48 hours in advance for Normal changes.
4. Execute with runbook and monitoring dashboard open.
5. Post-change verification: health checks, metrics, and a 24-72 hour observation period.

Rollbacks and automated safeguards:
- Every Normal/Standard change must include an automated rollback step.
- Canary + progressive rollout (5%, 25%, 100%) is mandatory for model or runtime changes impacting inference.

3) Data management
------------------
Goal: Protect customer and company data while enabling teams to use data for product, monitoring, and billing.

Classification:
- Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted.
- Sensitive data (PII, payment data, customer-provided private inputs) labeled Restricted.

Storage and access:
- All Restricted data must be stored in approved systems (encrypted at rest, KMS-managed).
- Access to Restricted data requires explicit approval and justification; use short-lived credentials where possible.

Data lifecycle:
- Retention policy table:
  - Logs (debug): 30 days
  - Monitoring metrics/aggregates: 13 months
  - Customer data (default): 90 days unless contract specifies otherwise
  - Audit logs: 7 years

Backups and recovery:
- Daily backups for customer-critical datasets; test restore quarterly.

Data sharing and exports:
- Data exports containing Restricted data require a Data Export Request with security and legal approval. Exports must be encrypted in transit and at rest and tracked in the data exports register.

Incident response and breaches:
- Suspected data exposure must follow Incident Response Security flow in /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security. Notify security within 1 hour of discovery.

4) Procurement & expense processing
----------------------------------
Goal: Ensure economically responsible spending with consistent approval and reconciliation.

Procurement thresholds and approvers:
- <= $2,000: Manager approval.
- $2,001- $25,000: Department head approval + Finance notification.
- > $25,000: Finance + Legal procurement review and VP-level approval.

Preferred vendors and purchase process:
- Use the company procurement portal for purchases tied to purchase orders. For SaaS or cloud spend, consult the FinOps playbook for preferred SKUs and reserved capacity options.

Expense reporting and reimbursement:
- Employees use the expense system (link: /expenses) with receipts attached within 30 days.
- Corporate cards: monthly reconciliation required by cardholder with manager sign-off.

Supplier onboarding (procurement + legal):
1. Raise a Purchase Request with business justification and budget code.
2. Finance verifies budget and issues PO where required.
3. Legal reviews contract for data, SLAs, and indemnities.
4. Finance closes the loop after invoice reconciliation.

5) Vendor management
--------------------
Goal: Maintain a central inventory of vendors, assess risk, and ensure contractual compliance.

Vendor classification:
- Critical (core infra, cloud providers, model hosts)
- Strategic (multi-year partnerships)
- Standard (tools, SaaS)

Minimum onboarding checklist:
- Completed Vendor Intake Form
- Security questionnaire (for access to systems or data)
- Signed contract reviewed by Legal
- Data processing addendum (DPA) when vendor processes customer data

Ongoing reviews and SLAs:
- Critical vendors: quarterly performance and security reviews.
- All vendors: annual contract and risk review. Maintain vendor scorecard in Procurement system.

Offboarding vendors:
- Revoke access, collect assets, ensure data deletion per contract, and confirm final invoice reconciliation.

6) Travel policy
----------------
Goal: Safe, economical, and compliant travel for business needs.

Booking and approvals:
- Travel must be pre-approved using the Travel Request form with estimated costs and justification. Managers approve trips and budget code.
- Use preferred travel vendors and corporate rates where available.

Expenses and per-diems:
- Reimbursable items: airfare (economy unless pre-approved), lodging (standard single room), meals, ground transport, and reasonable incidentals.
- Non-reimbursable: personal upgrades, entertainment beyond company-approved client meals without prior approval.

Safety and compliance:
- Employees traveling to high-risk regions must get Travel Security sign-off and register travel dates.
- Emergency contact and local embassy information must be provided for international trips.

7) Internal templates and record-keeping
-------------------------------------
Available templates (Confluence/template library):
- Access Request form
- Change Request template (change window, rollback plan, verification steps)
- Procurement request / vendor intake form
- Travel request and expense template
- Data Export Request and DPA checklist

Record retention and auditability:
- All approvals (access, change, procurement) must be recorded in the linked ticketing system.
- Maintain an auditable trail for a minimum of 3 years for financial and procurement records; security-related logs may be retained longer as specified in Data Management.

Appendix: Quick checklists
-------------------------
Access request checklist:
- Manager approval obtained
- Technical owner signed off
- Expiry date set
- IAM ticket created

Change request checklist:
- Rollback plan documented
- Monitoring dashboards identified
- Stakeholders notified
- Post-change verification steps provided

Procurement checklist:
- Budget verified
- PO/contract present
- Legal reviewed for data clauses (if applicable)

Contacts and escalation matrix
----------------------------
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com
- Security: security@redwood.com
- Finance: finance@redwood.com
- Legal: legal@redwood.com
- IT / IAM: iam@redwood.com
